Matt Barnes Finally Reveals the Truth Behind His Infamous Kobe Bryant ‘No-Flinch’ Moment

SG King | Sep 17, 2026
FacebookTweetThreadsReddit
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:17
Instaread

More than 16 years later, Matt Barnes still gets asked about one of the most replayed moments of his NBA career — and it didn’t even involve a shot, dunk or hard foul.

It happened on March 7, 2010, during a heated game between the Orlando Magic and Los Angeles Lakers.

Barnes was inbounding the basketball directly in front of Kobe Bryant when he suddenly faked as if he were about to fire the ball straight into Bryant’s face.

Kobe didn’t move.

He didn’t duck.

He didn’t blink.

At least that’s how the moment appeared on camera, and the clip quickly became another piece of Bryant’s legendary on-court mythology.

Now Barnes is looking back on the viral confrontation and the remarkable relationship that developed between the two competitors afterward.

Barnes Admits He Wanted to Fight Kobe

Speaking recently with NBA reporter Scoop Robinson, Barnes reflected on just how intense things became between him and Bryant that afternoon.

“We laughed at it. I wanted to fight Kobe and I told him, too,” Barnes said. “Actually, I told him in our last interview. Just competitors.”

That competitive element is important.

Barnes built his NBA reputation as a physical, emotional player who wasn’t interested in backing down from anybody.

Bryant operated with much the same mentality.

Put those personalities opposite each other in a competitive game, and there was always a chance something memorable would happen.

On that March afternoon, it did.

The Fake Pass Became an Instant Kobe Moment

The sequence itself was remarkably simple.

Barnes stood out of bounds preparing to inbound the basketball while Bryant guarded the play.

Barnes suddenly brought the ball toward Bryant’s face as if he were going to throw it directly at him.

Bryant appeared completely unfazed.

The Lakers superstar remained in position while Barnes pulled the ball back.

It lasted only a second, but the clip became one of the defining examples fans used when discussing Bryant’s legendary intensity.

For Kobe supporters, it was perfect.

A player tried to intimidate Bryant, and Bryant seemingly refused to give him even the satisfaction of a reaction.

There Was More Going On Than One Viral Clip

The famous inbound sequence wasn’t the only tense moment between Barnes and Bryant during the game.

The two spent much of the afternoon battling one another as Orlando and Los Angeles went at it.

There was physical contact, trash talk and plenty of competitive energy.

Barnes wasn’t trying to become part of a future internet meme.

He was trying to get under the skin of one of basketball’s fiercest competitors.

Bryant wasn’t interested in giving him the satisfaction.

That’s what made the matchup so entertaining.

Barnes Had Admired Kobe Long Before Their Confrontation

What sometimes gets lost when the famous clip resurfaces is that Barnes already had tremendous respect for Bryant.

Their relationship didn’t begin with that confrontation.

Barnes said he first had an opportunity to meet Bryant while Barnes was playing college basketball at UCLA.

“I got a chance to meet Kobe when I was at UCLA, and he was on campus all the time,” Barnes recalled.

For Barnes, Bryant represented something particularly important.

Barnes entered the NBA in an era when Michael Jordan’s career was winding down, meaning Bryant became the superstar he was able to personally compete against and measure himself against.

“I really admired him as a man and as a player,” Barnes said. “He was always the bar because I missed MJ.”

Kobe Became the Standard for Barnes

That comment helps explain why their battles became so meaningful to Barnes.

Bryant wasn’t simply another opposing shooting guard.

He represented the level Barnes wanted to test himself against.

If you could compete physically and mentally with Kobe Bryant, you knew exactly where you stood.

“So to be able to battle with him for so many years, have our incident, and then have him recruit me to the team… to go from teammates to brothers, and to share his last years with him was really special,” Barnes said.

That’s what makes the story so much more interesting than the original viral moment.

The two players went from nearly fighting each other to becoming teammates.

Kobe Eventually Helped Bring Barnes to the Lakers

Only months after their memorable confrontation, Barnes joined Bryant in Los Angeles.

Barnes signed with the Lakers ahead of the 2010-11 season and spent two years playing alongside the superstar he had been battling with Orlando.

It’s one of those NBA stories that almost feels too perfect.

A player gets into a heated confrontation with Bryant.

The confrontation becomes famous.

Then Bryant helps bring that same player onto his team.

For Barnes, it was evidence that Kobe understood the difference between competition and personal dislike.

Kobe Apparently Respected the Fire

Bryant wasn’t exactly known for wanting passive teammates.

He valued competitors.

Barnes had demonstrated that he wasn’t intimidated by Bryant’s reputation and wasn’t afraid to challenge him physically or verbally.

Instead of holding the Orlando confrontation against Barnes, Bryant apparently respected what he saw.

That’s a recurring theme in stories former players tell about Kobe.

He might battle someone relentlessly on the court, but that didn’t necessarily mean he disliked them afterward.

Sometimes the fight itself earned his respect.

Barnes certainly seems to view their confrontation that way now.

From Opponents to Teammates

Once Barnes arrived in Los Angeles, the relationship changed.

The player Barnes once wanted to fight became somebody he practiced with, traveled with and competed alongside.

Barnes had an opportunity to see Bryant’s preparation and intensity from an entirely different perspective.

Instead of trying to stop Kobe, he was now trying to help him win.

And according to Barnes, their relationship eventually developed well beyond basketball.

He described their evolution simply: from teammates to brothers.

Barnes Cherishes the Time He Had With Kobe

That part of the story carries considerably more weight today.

Bryant, his daughter Gianna and seven others died in a helicopter crash in January 2020.

For Barnes, memories that once represented competitive NBA stories now carry a completely different meaning.

The trash talk matters.

The confrontations matter.

The practices matter.

But so do the conversations and friendship that came afterward.

That’s why Barnes doesn’t look back at the famous fake-pass moment with resentment.

He laughs about it.

The Internet Turned the Moment Into Basketball History

The clip has taken on a life of its own over the years.

It gets reposted whenever fans discuss Bryant’s mentality.

It appears in highlight packages.

It circulates across social media.

And new generations of basketball fans who may never have watched the original game have still seen Barnes fake the basketball toward Kobe’s face.

That is the strange power of a viral sports moment.

An entire game can eventually fade from memory while one second lives forever.

Barnes Will Probably Never Escape the ‘No-Flinch’ Clip

Barnes has accomplished plenty beyond that one sequence.

He played 14 seasons in the NBA, suited up for numerous franchises and eventually won an NBA championship with the Golden State Warriors in 2017.

Since retiring, he has remained prominent in basketball media.

Yet mention Barnes and Bryant together, and many fans immediately picture the same moment.

Barnes has seemingly accepted that.

And considering how much Bryant eventually meant to him personally, there are probably worse things than being permanently connected to one of Kobe’s most famous displays of competitive intensity.

The Story Became Bigger Than the Beef

What looked like genuine hostility in 2010 eventually became the beginning of a much different relationship.

Barnes wanted to fight Bryant.

Bryant apparently respected Barnes enough to later want him on his team.

They became teammates.

Then friends.

Eventually, Barnes says, they became like brothers.

That’s the part a short viral clip can’t capture.

Fans see the ball fake.

Barnes remembers everything that came after it.

TMSPN Take

Kobe Bryant was one of a kind, and moments like this are exactly why his legend continues to live on.

It’s a shame he’s no longer here to sit down with Barnes and laugh about a confrontation that became part of NBA history.

The no-flinch clip will be replayed forever, but Barnes’ story about what happened afterward might be even better.
